title: primula farinosa subsp. fistulosa
intro: Primula farinosa subsp. fistulosa, commonly known as the marsh primrose, is a perennial plant species that belongs to the primrose family. It is known for its yellow flowers, which bloom in early spring and are often found in wetland areas. The marsh primrose has been traditionally used in herbal medicine due to its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The plant's bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, contribute to its therapeutic actions, including wound healing, anti-oxidative stress, and anti-inflammatory responses.
